findings.title: Rejected over-limit devices are cached before the DB call and bypass the limit afterward
findings.body: In tagDeviceUI the device's cache key is written with localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{}) *before* calling anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice. Now that TagDevice propagates the DB error (line 147) and client.go turns ErrDeviceLimitReached into a failed Authenticate, the failure happens after the cache is already populated. The local cache (localcache.New(29*time.Minute, ...)) therefore still holds the entry, so the next request from that same device hits the cache short-circuit at line 83, tagDeviceUI returns nil, TagDevice returns nil, and Authenticate succeeds. Result: a device that is over the configured limit is rejected only once per ~29-minute window and is otherwise granted anonymous access, defeating the feature. The cache key must only be set after a successful CreateOrUpdateDevice, or removed when the write fails.

findings.title: Device limit check is a non-atomic count-then-insert and can be exceeded under concurrency
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice performs a separate CountDevices query and then, if count < deviceLimit, does an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT/ON DUPLICATE KEY. These are two independent statements with no transaction or locking, so N concurrent requests for new device IDs all observe count == limit-1 and all insert, leaving the table with limit-1+N devices. The configured device_limit is therefore not a hard cap under bursty anonymous traffic. Enforcing the limit needs the count check and the insert to be atomic (e.g. a single conditional/transactional statement or a locking advisory lock).

findings.title: Device tagging is now synchronous on the anonymous auth path
findings.body: The previous code ran TagDevice in a detached goroutine with its own timeout so anonymous authentication did not block on the device store. It is now called synchronously with the request context inside Authenticate. For every anonymous request that misses the per-device cache this adds a database round trip to authentication: when device_limit > 0 it is at least a COUNT over anon_device plus an INSERT/UPDATE. On instances serving many distinct anonymous devices (public dashboards), this makes the login/auth path DB-bound and couples anonymous auth latency (and availability) to the anon_device table. The change should preserve the non-blocking behavior while still being able to enforce the limit (e.g. only reject after a synchronous existence/limit check that is cheap, or move the enforcement off the hot path).

findings.title: New auth.anonymous device_limit option is not documented
findings.body: A new config key device_limit is read from the [auth.anonymous] section (cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit = anonSection.Key("device_limit").MustInt64(0)), but no sample configuration (conf/defaults.ini / conf/sample.ini) or reference documentation for this option is added in this PR. Operators have no way to discover the setting, its default of 0 (unlimited), or its interaction with the 30-day device window. Add the option to the config sample and the authentication configuration docs.

findings.title: No test covers the limit enforcement through the service/cache path
findings.body: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only exercises AnonDBStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice directly and asserts the second insert returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. There is no test that drives TagDevice/Authenticate for an over-limit device, which is exactly where the localCache ordering bug (cache set before write) makes the limit unenforced on subsequent requests. Add a test that goes through the Anonymous/AnonDeviceService path and verifies a rejected device stays rejected, and that a device under the limit still succeeds.
